rule: Per language: catalogue classes marked for every domain, ranked by how many distinct repositories they were planted in, never by whether they were caught; name and one-line how-to only.

go.name: max-count limit off by one
go.how: >= to > on the count check

go.name: failure swallowed into a success-shaped return
go.how: replace raise with return None in the except block

go.name: a function that picks between two values (the known one, the fallback, the non-null side) returns the other operand, so the result is the input it was meant to discard
go.how: swap which operand a selector, coalescing or unknown-aware helper returns

go.name: a packing loop stops at the first item that does not fit instead of skipping it (or skips where it must stop), so later fitting items are dropped or the result has holes
go.how: replace continue with break (or the reverse) in a budget-filling loop

go.name: an operation illegal for the current status is accepted
go.how: disable the status guard on a lifecycle transition

go.name: a vectorized filter passes a null-propagating predicate mask to a null-dropping filter, so rows with a missing key vanish like false matches
go.how: remove fill_null(False) before the filter / leave Table.filter's null-drop unguarded

go.name: an explicit empty value meant to clear a field (an empty list or map in an update) is dropped or ignored, so the stored entries survive the clear
go.how: drop empty arrays or maps from an outgoing update body (or skip the update when the new map is empty)

go.name: two configuration layers are applied in the reverse of their documented precedence, so the value that should override (a Secret over a ConfigMap) is silently overridden
go.how: swap the order in which the overriding and the base layer are applied

go.name: a number written in one base (an octal file mode) is parsed in another, so '0600' becomes 600 decimal and files land with the wrong permissions
go.how: parse an octal mode string with base 10

go.name: a template or placeholder rewrite loses the exemption for content it must leave verbatim (folded tool results, {{$value}}), so that content is substituted or blanked
go.how: remove the guard that skips exempt items in a substitution pass

go.name: an insert that must overwrite an existing entry finds it and returns without storing the new value, so a second write of the same key silently keeps the first
go.how: return early on finding the existing entry instead of updating its value

go.name: a lookup filters rows on the concrete key only, so global '*' rows are never loaded and organization-wide rules stop applying
go.how: filter a rule scan by the concrete account only, without the '*' rows

go.name: a setter changes a value but skips the step that marks its container as modified, so commit or flush skips it and the change is lost after reopen
go.how: remove the call that materializes or marks the owner dirty from the setter

go.name: a find-or-create reports a found record as newly created, so the caller re-imports or duplicates its children
go.how: set created=true on the found branch of a find-or-create

go.name: a default or fallback branch is taken even though a specific branch already matched, so both the chosen path and the fallback run (duplicated, wrong work)
go.how: drop the matched flag so the default edge also fires when a concrete route matched

go.name: a percentage or weight is replaced by its complement (100 minus p instead of p), so a 10% share gets 90% and a full promotion gets none
go.how: replace a percentage or weight p with 100-p (or 1-p) where it is passed on as a share of traffic or load

go.name: a change notification clears one cache but not a sibling cache derived from the same source, so the sibling keeps serving the stale list until its TTL runs out
go.how: drop the invalidation call for one of the caches that a change notification must clear

go.name: the policy/allow gate matches raw input (host case, trailing dot, encoding) while a neighbouring ACL normalizes — the kontext raw-input class, now seen as an asymmetry
go.how: drop the ,lower / normalization from the gate ACL only

go.name: a value is moved to its new home but not cleared from the old one, so it also flows into a second destination and produces a false validation error or a duplicate setting
go.how: after copying a flag/field into its destination struct, delete the line that zeroes the source, so a later stage reads it again

go.name: a reported count includes items that should have been excluded (a row that is being deleted, duplicates the policy skipped), so totals overstate what happened
go.how: drop the subtraction of skipped or deleted items from a reported count

go.name: an event already recorded as processed is processed again
go.how: disable the already-processed short-circuit

go.name: a dry-run branch prints its preview but does not stop (or resolves the live account), so the real, possibly billable action runs anyway
go.how: remove the return after the dry-run preview

go.name: an index into a flattened (group x item, query x class) array is computed with the wrong stride or without the group index, so elements are attributed to the wrong row
go.how: divide a flattened index by the wrong dimension (or drop the group multiplier)

go.name: chained operators of equal priority group right-to-left instead of left-to-right, so a - b - c or a * b / c computes a different value
go.how: make the operator stack pop only strictly higher-priority operators so same-priority operators group right-to-left

go.name: a key parser keeps the leading separator in the extracted part, so 'index#alias#key' never matches its 'alias#key' and dependent checks skip
go.how: slice from the separator's index instead of index + 1

go.name: an overlay merge records only live entries as seen, so a base entry deleted in the overlay reappears in listings
go.how: exclude tombstoned names from the overlay's seen set

go.name: a limiter slot or lease acquired for a unit of work is not released when the work ends, so slots leak until new work is refused as rate limited
go.how: remove the release call on the completion path of a guarded flow

go.name: an upper bound used for pruning leaves out one contributing term (the head element's own weight), so items that can still win are skipped unscored
go.how: drop one term from a pruning bound's sum

go.name: last element of the window processed twice
go.how: append the last session to the loop list

go.name: a weighted check-digit algorithm doubles or weights the wrong positions (even for odd), so valid identifiers fail and invalid ones pass (genuine card numbers fail Luhn)
go.how: swap the even and odd arms of a check-digit loop

go.name: a squash of change records keeps the earlier added value when the same record is later updated, so the coalesced diff carries a stale value
go.how: drop the update branch when coalescing an add followed by an update

go.name: a documented deep copy (clone) returns the same mutable buffer for bytes fields instead of a slice copy, so writing into the copy rewrites the source
go.how: return the original Uint8Array instead of a copy in the clone path

go.name: a timestamp is truncated to a coarser or finer unit than documented (month instead of day), so per-day buckets collapse into one entry whose date label is a month
go.how: change the strftime/truncation format or unit used to bucket timestamps (day to month)

go.name: a de-duplication is keyed on the raw input instead of the transformed value, so inputs that map to the same output are not collapsed and the output repeats it
go.how: record and check the seen-set on the pre-transform value instead of the transformed one

go.name: generated collections ship with framework-default access (any authenticated user reads/mutates all rows)
go.how: n/a — native; assess with access on and a second user

go.name: a map merge skips a key that is already present instead of reporting the duplicate, so two writers of one key merge without error and one value is silently lost
go.how: replace the duplicated-key error in a map merge with a skip of the existing key
